Inglewood, California
  January 22, 2019

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on
Tuesday, January 22, 2019, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into session for Closed Session at the hour of
1:00 p.m.

The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales, and Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.

City officials and personnel present for Closed Session were as follows:

  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney
  Patricia McNish  Management Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEMS. Mayor
Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City
Council on the Closed Session Item.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:01 p.m. for Closed Session
Item No. CS-1.

  **********************************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called
the City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency and .Housing
Authority at the hour of 2:00 p.m.
The City Clerk/ Successor Agency Secretary/ Housing Authority Secretary
announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority  Chairman  Butts,  Council
  Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales and
  Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.
City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
follows:
  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Wanda Brown  City Treasurer/Treasurer*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO
  Patricia McNish  Management Assistant

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency and Housing Authority.

  1
 January 22, 2019

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons
  present who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing
  Authority on any item on the Agenda.

  There was no response.

 180  PRESENTATION. Mayor Butts acknowledged Anthony Porter, an Inglewood
  Native, previously incarcerated former Gang Member, and now works for the
  community based Organization called 2nd Call. According to Mr. Porter, 2nd Call
  assists Individuals in the Los Angeles and surrounding areas who are
  disenfranchised and individuals who society disregards.. Following a brief film
  presentation, Mayor Butts presented the 2nd Call members with certificates
  praising them for being hard working citizens dedicated to Society and the
  Community of Inglewood. Mr. Porter also thanked the Mayor and Council
  members for all of their support.

 142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Franklin, and seconded
  by Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member
  Morales that the demands presented to the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority dated, January 18, 2019, in the amount of $71,391.44,
  dated January 18, 2019, in the amount of $4,780,545.41, are hereby allowed, and
  the City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is
  hereby authorized to certify upon said registers that said demands are so
  approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority
  Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor/Successor
  Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending
  denial of the following claims:
  a) Celia Chavez for alleged property damage on November 7, 2018.
  b) Consuelo Cordova for alleged personal injury and property damage on June 8,
  c) George Davison for alleged property damage on December 2, 2018.
  d) Regina Gilchrist for alleged property damage on July 24, 2018.
  e) Baltazar Gonzalez, Jr. for alleged personal injury and property damage on June
  8, 2018.
  f) Lillian Grant for alleged property damage on July 2, 2018.
  g) Luis Martin (3rd Claim) for alleged ADA Non-Compliance on October 11,
  2018.
  h) Passion Rodriguez for alleged property damage on December 8, 2018.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson and carried that the above listed claims be denied.

 301  4th AMENDMENT TO AGREEMENT NO. 10-68 APPROVED – PEARL
  MEDIA, LLC. Staff report dated January 22, 2019, was presented recommending
  approval of the Fourth Amendment to Agreement No. 10-68 with Pearl Media
  LLC, to extend the display of super graphic wall sign outdoor advertising.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby approve the Fourth Amendment to
  Agreement No. 10-68. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and;
  Noes: None.

  2
 January 22, 2019

 178  AGREEMENT NO. 19-094 APPROVED – LAWLES ENTERPRISES;
  PAYMENT FOR PRIOR SERVICES RENDERED – AUTHORIZED;
  RESOLUTION NO. 19-26 ADOPTED – AMENDING FISCAL YEAR 2018-
  2019 BUDGET. Staff report dated January 22, 2019, was presented
  recommending approval of a three-year agreement (with an option to extend two
  (2) additional one (1) year terms) with Lawles Enterprises to perform background
  investigation services on behalf of the Police Department.

  It was moved by Council member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve agreement No. 19-04 in the
  amount of $100,000; 2) Authorize payment of an invoice in the amount of
  $19,600 for prior services rendered; and 3) Adopt Resolution amending the Fiscal
  Year 2018-2019 budget. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and;
  Noes: None.

 301  ORDINANCE NO. 19-06 ADOPTED – ADOPTING THE 2016
  CALIFORNIA TITLE 24 BUILDING CODES BY AMENDING AND
  DELETING VARIOUS SECTIONS AND ARTICLES OF CHAPER 11
  (BUILDING REGULATIONS), OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL
  CODE. Staff report dated January 22, 2019, was presented recommending
  adoption of Ordinance No. 19-06 to adopt California Title 24 Building Code.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following
  roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and;
  Noes:  None.

  Thereupon, it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that Ordinance No. 19-06 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA ADOPTING THE 2016 CALIFORNIA TITLE 24
  BUILDING CODES BY AMENDING AND DELETING
  VARIOUS SECTIONS AND ARTICLES OF CHAPTER 11
  (BUILDING REGULATIONS), OF THE INGLEWOOD
  MUNICIPAL CODE

  which was introduced at the meeting held on January 15, 2019, be adopted. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts
  and;
  Noes:  None.

 132.6  CLOSED SESSION – WORKERS COMPENSATION CLAIMS OF
  STEPHANIE FITZPATRICK VS. THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD. Closed
  Session - Confidential – Attorney/Client Privileged; City Council Conference
  with Legal Counsel regarding Anticipated Litigation Pursuant to Government
  Code Section 54956.9(d)(2); Workers Compensation Claims of Stephanie
  Fitzpatrick: Claim Nos. 20080110ING, 20080113ING, 20100032ING,
  2012005ING, and 20130104ING.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Franklin that the City Council does hereby authorize payment to settle up to $40,000.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts
  and;
  Noes: None.

  3
 January 22, 2019

 126  REMARKS - CITY CLERK. Yvonne Horton, City Clerk, congratulated and
  acknowledged Sabrina Barnes and her staff on doing an excellent job for the
  Martin Luther King, Jr. celebration held on January 19, 2019. The City Clerk also
  acknowledged Aisha Thompson, Deputy City Clerk, and her praise dancers,
  (GLADII), for their amazing job opening the Martin Luther King, Jr. celebration.
  Lastly, the City Clerk thanked the City Treasurer, Wanda Brown for attending the
  meeting regarding the upcoming Voters Centers.

 219  REMARKS – CITY TREASURER.  Wanda Brown, City Treasurer,
  congratulated Sabrina Barnes, Code Enforcement and Henry Brown on the
  success of the Martin Luther King, Jr. celebration. The City Treasurer also stated
  that a speech given at the MLK celebration, by a 7 year old boy was one of the
  best speeches she had ever heard. Lastly, the City Treasure congratulated 2nd Call
  and the wonderful job they are doing for previously incarcerated Men. The City
  Treasure also stated she is a part of an organization called “Different View”
  which assist newly released female parolees in getting their lives back together.
  .
  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City
  business not elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Matt Palmer, Supervisor of Electrical Engineers employed by the County
  Sanitation District of Los Angeles, representing AFSCME. Mr. Palmer discussed
  the Union issues and the status of ongoing Labor negotiations.

  Althea Moses, Inglewood Entrepreneur and Olympian, congratulated Sabrina
  Barnes on doing a wonderful job organizing the Martin Luther King, Jr.
  celebration. Ms. Moses also invited the Council Members and residents of
  Inglewood to her Fitness Class held on Tuesday and Thursday nights from
  6:30p.m. until 7:30p.m. at Darby Park. Lastly she stated she would like to start an
  organization called “Ready Achievers” in Inglewood to catch and assist the
  children before they leave High School.

  Willie Agee stated he is proud to live in the City of Inglewood. He also
  congratulated Sabrina Barnes and her staff for the wonderful job they did on the
  Martin Luther King, Jr. celebration. Mr. Agee stated that each year gets better and
  better.

  Erick Holly congratulated Sabrina Barnes for doing an amazing job putting on the
  Martin Luther King, Jr. celebration.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the
  meeting adjourned at 2:46 p.m.

  Approved this 5th day of February, 2019

  _________________________
  Yvonne Horton, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
